title: Mary's wisdom undoes Eve's fall

edition.locus: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Latin column, In annuntiationem Sermo I, printed p. 10, col. D, to p. 11, col. A (PDF pp. 34-35)

source_text: Nam prudens revera ac sapiens in cunctis erat: nec similis ei, ex universis generationibus ulla unquam est reperta. Non sicut antea virgo Eva sola in paradiso chorum agens atque tripudians, relaxata mente per incuriam ab Auctore omnis mali serpente, verbum suscepit; et sic sensu mentis corrupta est, ac per ipsam fraudulentus venenum effundens, mortemque admiscens, in omnem mundum introduxit: ac propterea omnis Sanctorum aerumna nata est: verum in sola sancta Virgine, eius lapsus reparatus est.
pass_a_gloss: For prudent (prudens) truly (revera) and wise (sapiens) in all things she was: nor like her (similis ei) from all generations (generationes) was any (woman) ever found (reperta est). Not as formerly (antea) the virgin Eve, alone (sola) in paradise (paradisus) leading the chorus (chorum agens) and dancing/leaping (tripudians), with mind relaxed (relaxata mente) through carelessness (incuria), from the author (auctor) of all evil, the serpent (serpens), received (suscepit) the word (verbum); and thus in the sense of her mind (sensu mentis) was corrupted (corrupta est), and through her the deceitful one (fraudulentus) pouring out (effundens) poison (venenum) and mixing in (admiscens) death (mors), into the whole world brought it in (introduxit): and on this account (propterea) all the hardship (aerumna) of the saints was born (nata est): but in the holy Virgin alone his/her fall (eius lapsus) was repaired (reparatus est).

choices.issue: She was not like the virgin Eve of old, who ... received the word
choices.choice: Eve is the subject of suscepit, so it is rendered 'She was not like the virgin Eve of old, who ... received the word', without adding a second receiving by Mary.
'eius lapsus' is ambiguous (Eve's fall, or the fall brought in through her); rendered 'that fall' to keep the ambiguity.

'sensu mentis corrupta' may echo 2 Corinthians 11:3 (Vulgate 'corrumpantur sensus vestri ... sicut serpens Evam seduxit'), and death brought into the world may echo Wisdom 2:24 or Romans 5:12; uncertain, not cited.
Margin variants 'al. prima virgo' and 'al. mente cordis' not adopted.

pass_b_english: For she was truly prudent and wise in all things, and no woman like her has ever been found among all the generations. She was not like the virgin Eve of old, who, alone in paradise, dancing and leaping, with her mind slackened through carelessness, received the word from the serpent, the author of all evil (Genesis 3:1-6), and so was corrupted in the understanding of her mind; and through her the deceiver, pouring out his poison and mingling death with it, brought it into the whole world. From this all the affliction of the saints was born. But in the holy Virgin alone that fall was repaired.
notes: 'Non sicut antea virgo Eva ... verbum suscepit' contrasts Mary with Eve; Eve is the subject of suscepit, so it is rendered 'She was not like the virgin Eve of old, who ... received the word', without adding a second receiving by Mary. 'eius lapsus' is ambiguous (Eve's fall, or the fall brought in through her); rendered 'that fall' to keep the ambiguity. Genesis 3:1-6 cited for the serpent and Eve. 'sensu mentis corrupta' may echo 2 Corinthians 11:3 (Vulgate 'corrumpantur sensus vestri ... sicut serpens Evam seduxit'), and death brought into the world may echo Wisdom 2:24 or Romans 5:12; uncertain, not cited. Margin variants 'al. prima virgo' and 'al. mente cordis' not adopted. 'ulla' (feminine) rendered 'no woman'.
source_notes: PDF p. 34 = printed p. 10, col. D, last line ('Nam prudens revera'), then PDF p. 35 = printed p. 11, col. A. Marginal variants: at 'virgo Eva' 'al. prima virgo'; at 'mentis' a variant reading roughly 'al. mente cordis' (small italic, uncertain). NOTE for existing section 1: the print ends that sentence 'solam gratia elegit' (p. 10 col. D); section 1 stops at 'solam.' and needs 'gratia elegit' added. This row starts after those words.
